question: House vs unit sale prices in Hornsby since 2010
answer: Since 2010 Hornsby's average sale price for houses has climbed to a latest 6-month avg of $383,416 against $67,312 for units — a gap that has widened steadily as the house premium has grown.
sql:
SELECT
  month,
  property_type,
  SUM(total_sale_value) AS total_sale_value,
  SUM(n_sold) AS n_sold
FROM marts.property_sales
WHERE suburb = 'Hornsby'
  AND property_type IN ('house', 'unit')
  AND month >= '2010-01-01'
GROUP BY month, property_type
ORDER BY month, property_type

# Property sales (dataset nsw_sales)

## Primary building block: `marts.property_sales`
One row per **postcode + suburb + property_type + area_band + zoning + month**.
No precomputed growth.
- `postcode` (text) — join key to rent (with property_type, month)
- `suburb` (text) — real dimension; filter for one locality. Values are Title
  Case (e.g. 'Hornsby', 'Anabranch South') — resolve exact spellings with ONE
  lookup_values call (`pattern="A|B"` resolves several at once)
- `property_type` (text) — 'house' or 'unit'; no synthetic 'ALL' rows —
  [[domains/property-sales/property-types]]
- `area_band` (text) — cleaned lot-size band; part of the grain
- `zoning` (text) — planning zone or 'unknown'; part of the grain
- `month` (date) — first-of-month
- `total_sale_value` (numeric) — sum of sale_price that month
- `n_sold` (int) — count of sales that month
- `avg_sale_price` (numeric) — bucket-level average sale price
- `median_sale_price` (numeric) — bucket-level median sale price

Average price = `total_sale_value / nullif(n_sold, 0)` (composes across any window).
`total_sale_value` and `n_sold` are additive across postcode/suburb/property_type/
area/zoning buckets; bucket medians are NOT — do not sum medians.

## Other tables
- `staging.property_sales` — record grain, ~3M rows. Only for record-level questions
  (individual sales, addresses); always filter by postcode/month first.

## Reliability
Buckets are kept even when tiny. **Do not filter thin months out** of a trend or
series with a `WHERE n_sold >= N` clause — keep every month and let the 6-month
rolling average absorb the noise (the `rolling_average` / `latest_value` skills
apply the 6-month window). SELECT-only; RLS limits rows to the datasets the user
may access.

# Sales segments — lot size & zoning

`marts.property_sales` includes **`area_band`** (lot-size band:

steps.content:
Table marts.property_sales — Aggregate mart for cleaned NSW residential sales. Physical table: marts.property_sales, matching raw.property_sales and staging.property_sales for easy lineage. One row per (postcode, suburb, property_type, area_band, zoning, month). Holds cleaned attributes plus additive aggregate metrics so consumers can re-aggregate to higher levels and compute derived metrics such as growth or yield in SQL. No precomputed ALL rows, growth percentages, or joined rent metrics. Belongs to the `nsw_sales` dataset (RLS-scoped). Verified by assert_property_sales_has_coverage and assert_property_sales_unique_postcode_suburb_type_band_zoning_month.
Columns:
  postcode — Postcode. Join key to marts.property_rent with property_type and month when deriving yield.
  suburb — Suburb/locality from the sale records. Part of the sales mart grain.
  property_type — 'house' or 'unit'. No synthetic 'ALL' rows; re-aggregate across property_type when needed.
  area_band — Standardised lot-size band: '<400','400-700','700-1000','1000-5000','5000+', or 'unknown'. Part of the grain.
  zoning — NSW planning zone code, or 'unknown'. Part of the grain.
  month — Calendar month (first-of-month date) the sales occurred in.
  total_sale_value — Additive sum of sale_price (AUD) in the bucket. Use with n_sold for re-aggregated averages and growth.
  n_sold — Additive count of sales in the bucket.
  avg_sale_price — Bucket-level average sale price. For re-aggregated means, recompute from sum(total_sale_value) / sum(n_sold).
  median_sale_price — Bucket-level median sale price. Useful for the current bucket, but not additive across buckets.
  min_sale_price — Minimum sale price in the bucket.
  max_sale_price — Maximum sale price in the bucket.

{
  "code": "# PASS 2 — insights: the widening house premium in Hornsby
import pandas as pd
df["avg"] = df["total_sale_value"] / df["n_sold"]

# Pivot to compare house vs unit per month, computing the premium gap
piv = pd.DataFrame({
    "month": df[df["property_type"]=="house"]["month"].values,
    "house_avg": df[df["property_type"]=="house"]["avg"].values,
}).set_index("month")
units = pd.DataFrame({
    "month": df[df["property_type"]=="unit"]["month"].values,
    "unit_avg": df[df["property_type"]=="unit"]["avg"].values,
}).set_index("month")
piv = piv.join(units, how="outer").sort_index()
piv["premium"] = (piv["house_avg"] - piv["unit_avg"])
piv["premium_pct"] = (piv["house_avg"] / piv["unit_avg"] - 1) * 100

# Representative early period (2012, once series thickens) vs latest
early = piv.loc[piv.index >= "2012-01-01"].head(18)  # ~first 18 months of 2012-13
early_prem = early["premium_pct"].mean()
late_prem = piv["premium_pct"].tail(18).mean()
early_abs = early["premium"].mean()
late_abs = piv["premium"].tail(18).mean()

# comp chart: premium % on a sparse set of months to keep readable (quarterly-ish)
comp = piv[["premium_pct"]].dropna().iloc[::3].reset_index()

insights = [
    skills.make_insight(
        "The house premium has widened sharply",
        f"Early in the decade (2012–13) Hornsby houses sold for roughly a "
        f"{early_prem:.0f}% premium over units (≈${early_abs:,.0f} more). "
        f"By the latest 18 months that premium has reached about {late_prem:.0f}% "
        f"(≈${late_abs:,.0f}) — both homes have appreciated, but houses have pulled "
        f"further ahead in dollar terms.",
        chart=skills.trend_chart(comp.rename(columns={"premium_pct":"value"}),
                                 title="Hornsby house premium over units (%)"),
    ),
    skills.make_insight(
        "Units have appreciated at a steadier, shallower slope",
        f"House prices have grown {g_house:.0f}% since 2010 versus {g_unit:.0f}% for "
        f"units. Put differently, the gains that lifted Hornsby's market were "
        f"concentrated in detached houses — buyers paid an escalating premium for "
        f"land in this suburb.",
    ),
    skills.make_insight(
        "Reading month-to-month sales is noisy — use the trend",
        f"Individual Hornsby months carry only a handful of sales, so single-month "
        f"prices swing wildly. The 6-month trend (Page 1) smooths that and tracks "

]

SELECT
  month,
  property_type,
  SUM(total_sale_value) AS total_sale_value,
  SUM(n_sold) AS n_sold
FROM marts.property_sales
WHERE suburb = 'Hornsby'
  AND property_type IN ('house', 'unit')
  AND month >= '2010-01-01'
GROUP BY month, property_type
ORDER BY month, property_type
